certificate_method.published_method_not_read: the reference chapter 'Successive Difference Substitution' in Xia and Yang's book (DOI 10.1142/9789814759120_0010) was not read, so this is a sound subset of the idea rather than a reproduction of the algorithm
certificate_method.substitution: the j-th smallest variable becomes the sum of the first j+1 difference variables
certificate_method.why_incomplete: coefficient positivity after one substitution is a sufficient condition only; a statement no ordering certifies is Unknown
certificate_method.why_sound: on the ordered cone that substitution is exactly the change to nonnegative difference variables, so nonnegative coefficients give nonnegativity there; every nonnegative point sorts into some ordering, so taking all n! orderings gives the whole orthant

cost.note: the wall time is measured and is not part of any retained claim

naive_iteration.conclusion: applying the substitution again proves nonnegativity only on the sub-cone where the differences are themselves ordered, which is strictly smaller, so naive iteration does not strengthen the certificate
naive_iteration.second_substitution_needs: the difference variables themselves to be ordered
naive_iteration.what_is_measured: whether substituting twice certifies the same statement on the same cone

schur_t1.what_this_shows: Schur's inequality has both kinds of certificate: the ordered one here, which a reader can check by the sign of five factors, and the substitution one. The marginal-wall inequality has only the first kind, which is why the two kinds are kept apart

amgm3.note: the polynomial form of AM-GM for three terms

amgm4.note: the four-variable case, which exercises all 24 orderings

false_companion_power_mean.note: fails at x=y=z=1, where the value is -1

marginal_wall_discriminant.claim: cs^2 k^2 - (2 cs kappa - s) k + kappa^2 >= 0 for cs,kappa,k,s >= 0, with g = 2 cs kappa - s
marginal_wall_discriminant.note: the discriminant inequality of the repository's marginal-wall round; equality of the two forms is checked exactly

motzkin.note: the Motzkin polynomial: nonnegative, and not a sum of squares of polynomials

nesbitt.note: multiplied by 2(x+y)(y+z)(z+x), which is positive on the open orthant

schur_t1.claim: Schur t=1: sum_cyc x(x-y)(x-z) >= 0, that is x^3+y^3+z^3+3xyz >= sum_sym x^2 y
schur_t1.note: a classical symmetric inequality on the orthant; the first version of this statement was mis-written as x^3+y^3+z^3+xyz >= xy(x+y)+yz(y+z)+zx(z+x), which is FALSE at (1,1,1), and the corrected form is used here

statement_error.corrected_to: sum_cyc x(x-y)(x-z) >= 0, that is x^3+y^3+z^3+3xyz >= sum_sym x^2 y
statement_error.what_was_written: x^3+y^3+z^3+xyz >= xy(x+y)+yz(y+z)+zx(z+x), which is false at (1,1,1) with value -2
statement_error.why_it_matters: a sampling soundness audit did not catch it, because random orthant points essentially never have three equal coordinates; the corrected statement and the witness search are the response

weitzenbock.claim: (a^2+b^2+c^2)^2 >= 3(a+b+c)(-a+b+c)(a-b+c)(a+b-c), which is 48 times the squared area
weitzenbock.note: sides written as y+z, z+x, x+y, which turns the triangle condition into x,y,z >= 0

sum_of_squares_identity.sos_form: cs^2 k^2 - (2 cs kappa - s) k + kappa^2 = (cs k - kappa)^2 + s k
sum_of_squares_identity.what_this_shows: the repository's marginal-wall inequality has an exact sum-of-squares certificate even though the difference substitution does not certify it within one round

motzkin_is_certified.expected: Unknown, because the Motzkin polynomial is the classical example of a nonnegative polynomial that is not a sum of squares
motzkin_is_certified.kept: cited as a finding about what this certificate reaches; the classical non-sum-of-squares fact is cited and not verified in this run
motzkin_is_certified.measured: Certified by all six orderings, with an eighteen-term difference image whose coefficients are all nonnegative

the_repository_inequality_is_not_certifi.expected: either outcome, recorded as a measurement by the contract
the_repository_inequality_is_not_certifi.kept: the two certificates are different objects and the note keeps them apart
the_repository_inequality_is_not_certifi.measured: Unknown, with five negative coefficients in its difference image, while its sum-of-squares identity is exactly verified

the_schur_statement_was_mis_written_firs.expected: a certificate, because Schur's inequality is the standard textbook case
the_schur_statement_was_mis_written_firs.how_it_was_found: by evaluating the written statement at the symmetric point while preparing the ordered certificate, not by the sampling audit, which had passed because random orthant points essentially never have equal coordinates
the_schur_statement_was_mis_written_firs.kept: the mis-written statement, its false value at (1,1,1) and the fact that a sampling audit missed it are all retained; the run now searches a witness for every statement declared true, which is the check that would have caught it
the_schur_statement_was_mis_written_firs.measured_first: Unknown, because the statement had been written as x^3+y^3+z^3+xyz >= xy(x+y)+yz(y+z)+zx(z+x), which is FALSE: its value at (1,1,1) is -2

tooling.arithmetic: fractions.Fraction on sparse multivariate polynomials; no float in any certificate

what_is_not_claimed: This is an external exact computation, not a native certificate, and it admits nothing into any catalog
The published successive-difference-substitution algorithm was not read and is not reproduced; the reference is a chapter title and a DOI
A statement the certificate does not reach is Unknown, never false; the Motzkin polynomial is the concrete case here
The certificate is sound but incomplete, and its incompleteness is measured rather than bounded
The sum-of-squares identity is verified exactly, but it is an alternative certificate and not a product of the substitution
The classical fact that the Motzkin polynomial is not a sum of squares of polynomials is cited and not verified here, so the reach beyond the sum-of-squares cone rests on a cited premise
The soundness audit samples exact orthant points; it is evidence for the certificate, not a proof of it
Nothing here is claimed about non-polynomial inequalities, about inequalities outside an orthant, or about the published method's completeness
Nothing about Feigenbaum, Arakelov, mirror symmetry, the density-wave line beyond the one identity, or the repository's geometry growth line follows from this run
